checks.name: Markdown link portability
checks.description: Whether links in served markdown are absolute and resolve to what they promise
checks.message: 47 of 47 sampled markdown pages carry links that lose their target once the base URL is gone (root-relative links (47))
checks.resolution: 47 of 47 markdown pages link in a way that depends on the base URL (root-relative links on 47). Emit absolute URLs when generating markdown: the canonical host is known at build time, so absolute links cost nothing to produce. Root-relative links resolve only while the fetch URL is still around, and agent pipelines lose it routinely, to summarization, to RAG chunking, or to content being pasted somewhere else.

diagnostics.message: 11 generated pages show several symptoms of the same flattening problem. https://promptless.ai/blog/product-updates/suggestion-lifecycle-notifications: inconsistent (11% of the HTML content is missing from the markdown); unnavigable (5 of 6 links are relative). https://promptless.ai/blog/technical/parrots-are-underrated-pets-and-tools: inconsistent (15% of the HTML content is missing from the markdown); unnavigable (4 of 7 links are relative). https://promptless.ai/blog/technical/dogbench: inconsistent (5% of the HTML content is missing from the markdown); unnavigable (5 of 13 links are relative). And 8 more. Each check flags one symptom, but the cause is shared: the markdown variant is a second rendering pipeline, and it needs the same QA the HTML pipeline gets.
diagnostics.resolution: Treat these as one pipeline problem rather than separate findings. Review the generator that produces the agent-facing representation of the affected pages for how it dumps widget data, whether it inherits UI pagination or a default filter, and how it writes links, then re-run embedded-data-serialization, single-fetch-completeness, markdown-content-parity, and markdown-link-portability together on those pages.
